description: Professional advice received, recorded so that a disagreement with the statute is visible rather than silent — and so that reliance on advice is provable if it later proves wrong.
why_record_advice: A conflict between advice and the rules should be a decision the operator makes knowingly, not one that passes unnoticed.
Where advice turns out to be wrong, a contemporaneous record of having relied on it in good faith matters — for penalty proceedings, and for deciding whether to keep the adviser.
An adviser may be right for reasons the rule set does not encode. 'Conflict' means look at this, never 'the adviser is wrong'.
how_to_add: Record the advice verbatim where possible, with date, adviser and source. Add a `claim` only where the advice makes a machine-checkable assertion; otherwise leave it out and the entry is kept for the audit trail alone.

advice.subject: TDS on ARTH's own audit fee — first position
advice.advice: The TDS liability u/s 194J arises for the professional fees paid in excess of Rs. 50,000/-. Hence, in this case, there is TDS payable of Rs. 12,500/- along with interest of Rs. 750/-. Request you to kindly pay this amount to facilitate the filing of return.
advice.note: This position is correct and matches the encoded rule exactly.

advice.source: email, same thread, 11:11 UTC — 73 minutes after A001
advice.subject: TDS on ARTH's own audit fee — position withdrawn
advice.advice: As discussed over the phone, please ignore the previous email. Tax is not deducted since the company already has significant accumulated losses of this expense will not have a material impact.

claim.rule_position: Accumulated losses do not remove a deductor's liability. Losses bear on the s.40(a)(ia) disallowance of the expense; the obligation to deduct and deposit under s.194J, and liability as assessee-in-default under s.201, are unaffected by either party's profitability.
claim.authority: Income-tax Act 2025 s.393(1) (old s.194J); s.201; s.40(a)(ia)
claim.why: Two distinct consequences of non-deduction were conflated: the disallowance (which losses do affect) and the deductor's primary liability (which they do not). Note also that the adviser was the payee of the fee in question.

advice.outcome: Followed at the time. The ₹12,500 remains undeposited and interest has accrued since 07-11-2025.
advice.note: The conflict this whole mechanism exists to surface. Recorded as lesson L003.

advice.source: email accompanying invoice ARTH 371, FY 2024-25 statutory audit
advice.subject: Request not to deduct TDS on their invoice
advice.advice: Please note that since we have accumulated losses so no TDS was considered on this invoice and hence request to consider the full gross amount for release without deducting TDS.

claim.rule_position: A payee's accumulated losses are not a ground for non-deduction. Only a certificate under s.197 (lower or nil deduction) authorises paying gross, and none was produced.
claim.why: A written request from the payee to skip a statutory deduction, on grounds that have no basis in the section.

advice.outcome: Complied with — ₹1,47,500 paid gross on 13-10-2025, no TDS deducted.
advice.note: Same reasoning as A002, offered three months earlier and in writing.

advice.subject: Why no Form 16 existed for FY 2024-25
advice.advice: When filing the individual ITRs for FY 2024-25, we discussed that Form 16 was unavailable because the tax was not deducted. Furthermore, 30% of the salary expense was disallowed in the...
advice.note: Not a machine-checkable claim, but evidence that the same reasoning — accept the 30% disallowance instead of deducting — was applied to salary TDS as well, not only to the adviser's own fee. Relevant context for any assessment of the pattern.
